messages:
sam.procure: Vendor M sent a pilot invoice + terms. Two flags: they want pilot credits to be "stackable" across projects but exclude EMEA-resident data from credits. Also their amendment window is 90 days. Thoughts?

ana.finance: that's risky. Excluding EMEA data from credits kills our EU rollout economics. paste snippet if you can.

sam.procure: snippet from terms: "Pilot credits are stackable across accounts but are not applicable to services ingesting data stored in EU jurisdictions. Credits expire 90 days after invoice."

julia.sales: 90 days is too long to tie credits — we need an amend window of 30 days max. Also stackable credits are fine if they count toward year-1 commit. Ask for conversion cap 65% of unused credits to year-1 commit.

omar.billing: operational issues: VAT treatment differs by jurisdiction. If credits cannot apply to EU invoices, we'll have split accounting entries. Need vendor to confirm tax treatment and provide example credit memo for EU/Germany. Also require a single credit memo ID to avoid double-counting.

vendorbot: Vendor M uploaded terms v2: https://vendorm.example.com/terms/2026-03-eu (v2)

sam.procure: propose reply: 1) credits must apply to all jurisdictions where we ingest data (including EU), 2) amendment window 30 days, 3) allow conversion of up to 65% of unused pilot credits to year-1 prepayment upon signed amendment, 4) vendor must supply EU invoice examples and a single credit memo ID, 5) SOC2 Type II or equivalent EU attestation before any EU data ingestion. If they won't do 1), limit pilot to non-EU data.

ana.finance: add audit right for 12 months and require the conversion clause: "Converted pilot credits shall be treated as prepayments reducing committed fees dollar-for-dollar and documented via a single credit memo." Also insist on sample journal entries for AP/tax.

julia.sales: I'll push the rep. If vendor resists on EU, offer a scoped EU pilot with higher credits but shorter amendment window.

omar.billing: once vendor provides sample credit memo and VAT treatment, i'll sign-off on AP entries. Until then we hold disputed onboarding/enablement fees.

sam.procure: thanks. sending the asks now and requesting corrected invoice showing any waived enablement fees. Will update thread when they reply. :email:
